message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Why you might choose it |
|--------|-----------------|-------------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, interactive, automatically handles authentication, scopes, and metadata. |
| **REST API (curl)** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/...` | Useful if you’re building a programmatic workflow or integrating with another system. |

> **Important prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled.  
> * Enable the **Compute Engine API** (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * Request a GPU quota for the **nvidia-a6000** accelerator in the zone you plan to use.  
> * Install the NVIDIA driver on the instance after it boots (see the startup‑script below).  

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Variables – change these to match your environment
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM – adjust as needed
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT_ID" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --service-account="$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="displayName:default" --format="value(email)")"
```

### `startup.sh` – install NVIDIA drivers automatically

Create a file named `startup.sh` in the same directory:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Update package lists
apt-get update

# Install NVIDIA driver (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS)
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to load the driver
reboot
```

> The `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` flag tells Compute Engine to run this script at first boot, installing the driver and rebooting the VM.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (curl)

> **Prerequisites**  
> * Obtain an OAuth 2.0 access token with the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform` scope.  
> * Replace placeholders (`{project}`, `{zone}`, `{token}`) with your values.

```bash
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "$(gcloud iam service-accounts list --filter="displayName:default" --format="value(email)")",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
EOF

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

### What the JSON does

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `disks` | Boot disk image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS) and size |
| `guestAccelerators` | Adds the RTX A6000 GPU |
| `networkInterfaces` | Default VPC + external IP |
| `serviceAccounts` | Grants full Cloud Platform access |
| `metadata` | Startup script that installs NVIDIA driver |
| `tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules |

---

## Quick Checklist

1. **Project & Billing** – Confirm project ID and billing enabled.  
2. **GPU Quota** – Verify you have a quota for `nvidia-a6000` in the chosen zone.  
3. **Firewall Rules** – The tags `http-server` and `https-server` open ports 80/443; adjust if needed.  
4. **Driver Installation** – The startup script installs driver `535`; you can change the version if required.  
5. **Reboot** – The script reboots the VM so the driver loads; you can remove the reboot if you prefer manual restart.

Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh ubuntu@$EXTERNAL_IP
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy computing!
